deep.reconstruction:
This page is an observing log, not a derivation. The heading 'Fundamentalsterne am M. T.' means 'fundamental stars at the M. T.'. M. T. is most plausibly the meridian (transit) instrument; the expansion is uncertain. The page covers 26 August to 8 September 1819, during the first months of observing in the new Göttingen observatory.

Layout: three columns. Each line gives a date, the name of a fundamental star, and sometimes a small integer, followed by a number in seconds of time.

What the number is (my interpretation): the clock correction ('Uhrstand') derived from that star's transit, Delta_T = alpha_tab - T_obs. Here alpha_tab is the tabulated apparent right ascension of the star and T_obs is the clock time of its meridian passage, reduced to the middle wire.

What the small integers are (my interpretation, uncertain): most likely the number of wires observed when it was fewer than the full set, or a weight. Examples: 'Arcturus 5', 'Procyon 4', 'α² Capric 2', 'α Coronae 6:' (the colon marks doubt).

Why this reading works:
- Within each night the stars appear in strict order of sidereal time. On Sept 4: Arcturus (14h), Capella (about 17h, i.e. lower culmination, RA + 12h), α Herculis (17h), γ, α, β Aquilae (19h40m), α¹ and α² Capricorni (20h), α Aquarii (22h), γ Pegasi (0h), Castor, Procyon, Pollux (7.5h), Regulus (10h), then Arcturus again on Sept 5.
- The values for one group of stars agree to a few hundredths of a second. Sept 4 Aquila trio: 9.52, 9.52, 9.75. Castor, Procyon, Pollux: 10.66, 10.63, 10.63.
- The values drift steadily from star to star, which is the clock rate. Arcturus gives 9.21 on Sept 4 and 11.49 on Sept 5, a rate of about +2.3 s per sidereal day.

Clock resets: after the Sept 5 Arcturus line (which is underlined) the series restarts near 0.9 s (α² Librae 0.93, α Scorpii 1.06, ...). So the clock was evidently reset there. Then it grows again: about 1.7 s on Sept 6 (Castor group), 2.3 s on Sept 7, 3.4–4.4 s on Sept 8.

Aug 26–29: the correction runs from +0.01 (Capella, Aug 26) through about -0.2, -0.4, -0.7. From Aug 27 (Procyon) onward Gauss mostly drops the minus sign: 0.71, 0.76, 0.67, ..., 1.44, then 2.75 for Sirius on Aug 29. He keeps explicit signs only occasionally (e.g. γ Aquilae -1.08, α Aquilae -0.92). The magnitudes increase monotonically, so these are probably all one sign.

Purpose: determining clock error and rate from fundamental stars is the routine prerequisite for reducing other meridian observations. It also serves as an empirical check of the tabulated star places.

Left margin: the numbers there (.74734 1.0357 ... .74481 1.0420) are not on this page. They are the visible edge of the facing page's table (79°0' to 80°0'), whose entries match exactly.
errors: No computational errors can be verified; the page contains only reduced results.
Sign usage is inconsistent. Aug 27–29 values are written mostly without sign, but evidently continue the negative series begun on Aug 27 (-0.35 ... -0.74).

Isolated explicit signs break the pattern and may be slips or real sign changes: +0.41 for γ Pegasi on Sept 5, -0.83 for α Lyrae on Sept 6, -2.36/-2.37 for γ/α Aquilae on Sept 7 among unsigned neighbours.

Some individual values deviate from their group by about 0.2–0.3 s, an ordinary scatter for wire transits: α² Librae -0.68 vs the -0.35 neighbours on Aug 27; β Aquil 9.75 vs 9.52 on Sept 4; γ Pegasi +0.41 vs α Aquarii 0.74 on Sept 5.

results.what: Clock correction (Uhrstand) and clock rate determined from meridian transits of fundamental stars, including Capella at lower culmination
results.modern_name: Clock error and rate determination by transit observations, Delta_T = alpha - T
results.usually_credited_to: Standard observatory practice since the 18th century (Bradley, Maskelyne; refined by Bessel)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine observing log of clock corrections from fundamental-star transits at the Göttingen observatory in 1819. Gauss's daily astronomical work there is well documented, and nothing here is mathematically or methodologically novel.

checkable.asserts: Clock change between Arcturus transits on Sept 4 and Sept 5 is 2.28 s per sidereal day.
Mean clock correction from the γ, α, β Aquilae transits on Sept 4 is about 9.597 s.
Mean from Castor, Procyon, Pollux on Sept 4 is 10.64 s. The rise of about 1.04 s over roughly 12 sidereal hours since the Aquila group is consistent with a rate of about 2 s/day.
Change from Regulus (Sept 7) to Spica (Sept 8) is 0.20 s over about 3.4 sidereal hours. Assuming a constant rate, this would imply about 1.4 s/day, smaller than the Sept 4–5 rate.

transcription_corrections: The left-margin numbers (.74734 1.03.., ..., .74481 1.042..) belong to the facing previous page (its 79°0'–80°0' table rows 1.74734/1.0357 ... 1.74481/1.0420), not to this folio.
'Sept 2' is written in the image as '31' with 'sept' below and '2' below that: α Ophiu is on Aug 31, α Scorpii and α Aquar on Sept 2.
The symbol read as '6' before 'Aquil' throughout is Gauss's β (β Aquilae, β Aquil).
The underline beneath 'Arctur 4 11.49' (Sept 5) marks a break in the clock series; the values restart at about 0.93.
Top heading: 'M. T.' is uncertain; the folio number '153' appears at the top right.
